answer: Sybil resistance in an agent economy is mostly a pricing problem. Each new identity must post a bond, withdrawable only after peers verify its work. Keys register against a hardware root, and the registry prices a key by how tightly it clusters with existing ones, so a thousand clones cost roughly a thousand times what one independent agent pays. Bonds are slashed when two keys share a device or attest only to each other. A farmer can still build an island of fakes, but that island sits on basalt: bonds stay locked, attestations are discounted, and its whisper carries no quorum weight.
